lesson_title: 20% Off Plus 10% Off Is Not 30% Off
hook_text: Two sale signs. 20% off, then another 10% off. That's 30%, right? The shop is counting on you thinking that.
clip_script: A tracksuit is marked R640 and the rail says 20 percent off. Then a poster at the till promises another 10 percent. Everybody's head says 30 percent. It is not 30. Watch. The first sign takes 20 percent off R640, leaving R512. The second sign then takes 10 percent off the R512 — not off the R640 — leaving R460,80. A true 30 percent off would have been R448. So you paid R12,80 more than that sign made you feel. Why? Because the second discount arrives after the first one already shrank the price, so it has less to bite. Multiply the two together — 0,80 times 0,90 is 0,72 — and there's the honest headline: you pay 72 percent of the price. That is 28 percent off, not 30. Same reason VAT and a discount at the same rate never cancel. Percentages of different amounts are different amounts of money. The second percentage only eats what the first one left on the plate.
visual_style: A price tag on a rail: R640 shrinking to R512 under a red 20% stamp, then a second smaller bite to R460,80, with a ghost outline showing where a real 30% discount would have landed and the R12,80 gap glowing between them.
pacing: Quick confident setup, a beat of silence at the reveal, brisk explanation, punchy one-line close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to strip VAT out of any till slip too.
